findings.title: test-tools.sh doesn't hold two rules this commit states: the import walk reaching imports of imports, and traces dated only after a passed build. Either one reverted still passes all 41 checks
findings.scenario:
The README (182) says test-tools.sh checks the rules it lists for check.sh. check.sh's header (11-21) says two of them: every module of this package a listed module imports, "directly or not", is judged from its own trace; and traces are dated only "once a build passes". The test's fixture has no in-package chain two deep: Demo.Down imports Demo.Top, and Top imports only the dependency's Dep.Base. No case dates a trace after a failed build either. So two regressions each give 'PASS: the tools hold'.

(A) The walk cut to direct imports (check.sh:321). This quietly reopens l3tests#3 for 24 of lovejoin-any-tx's 48 unlisted imports, among them Lovejoin.V2.MixAny, MixAny3/4, MixSpec, MixTok2-4, OwnAny1-4 and their Spec modules, V2.Scripts, Lovejoin.Box and Steps, and Seedelf.Scripts, Scenario, Steps, Wallet and Policy. If one of them logged a sorry or an Undetermined, the run would read all ok and exit 0. The same cut loses lovejoin-v2-pools 12 of 16 imports, lovejoin-v2-outputs 21 of 28, lovejoin-owner 10 of 15 and audit-last 43 of 127.

(B) Traces dated after a failed, timed-out or killed build too (the guard is check.sh:345). Say Demo.Top's build times out before Lake rebuilds Demo.Imp, whose source was written with new bytes since its build. Imp's old trace gets dated, and tally.py and count.py then read its old log as current. The real tool keeps Imp STALE. Neither case is reachable today: these are the regressions the test exists to catch.
findings.evidence:
Lines are FIXTREE's (b0202c08).

The claims:
- check.sh:11-12 'Each module of this package that a module imports, directly or not, and the run doesn't list is read the same way'.
- check.sh:18-19 'Once a build passes, each trace read is dated to the build's start'.
- README.md:182 '`bash test-tools.sh` checks these rules in `check.sh`, …'.
- The commit: 'each of 22 mutants of the tools fails it'.

The fixture is make_pkg (test-tools.sh:62-82): Top imports Dep.Base and Blaster, Down imports Top, Side imports Dep.Base.

Base run on an unmodified copy (SCRATCH/r51/work/L4tools/tools): 41 ok, 'PASS: the tools hold', 4.6 s.

Mutant A: check.sh:321 `found.add(imp); todo.append(imp)` becomes `found.add(imp)`. `TOOLS=…/mut-direct bash test-tools.sh` gives PASS, exit 0. Harness /tmp/claude-1000/-home-logic-Documents-LogicalMechanism-Seedelf-Wallet/0e0d3674-7c6c-46fb-8cae-a49695fa3bfe/scratchpad/r51/work/L4tools/h-chain.sh: Top imports Mid, Mid imports Leaf, and Leaf's own trace has `declaration uses 'sorry'`.
- FIXTREE's check.sh: 'ok Demo.Top', 'SORRY Demo.Leaf (an import of Demo.Top, 1 sorry or native_decide)', '1 of 2 ok', exit 1.
- Mutant A: 'ok Demo.Top', '1 of 1 ok', exit 0.

A read-only emulation of judge()'s walk over FIXTREE's sources and traces (emulate_judge.py against diff_walk.py) gives 48 judged imports for lovejoin-any-tx with the transitive walk and 24 direct-only. It lists the 24 that are reached only transitively.

Mutant B: check.sh:371's failure branch gets `judge "$m" > /dev/null 2>&1` before forget. test-tools.sh gives PASS, exit 0. Harness h-timeout.sh: Top imports Imp, Imp.lean is dated 2026-11-12 against its trace's 2026-11-10, and lake exits 124.
- FIXTREE's: 'TIMEOUT Demo.Top', then tally.py 'NOT OK Demo.Imp: a trace older than its source (run ./check.sh on it)'.
- Mutant B: 'TIMEOUT Demo.Top', and tally.py reads 1 not ok (Top only), so Imp reads ok from its old log.

Three more survivors, each applied alone:
- check.sh:351 once-a-run `echo "$a" >> "$seenf"` dropped: PASS. A shared import is reported and counted twice.
- check.sh:296 `l == "warning" and` dropped: PASS. Blaster's info-level '✅ Expected Undetermined' (Smt/Env.lean:67-70) would read UNDETERM. No trace in FIXTREE has one.
- check.sh:298 sorryAx dropped: PASS. Only the compiler axioms are exercised.

Controls that fail as they should: dating to judge()'s own clock ('FAIL a source written during its build reads fresh'), and dating only the listed module ('FAIL a replayed module still reads stale').
findings.fix:
Add an in-package chain two deep to the fixture, such as Demo.Leaf imported by Demo.Top:
- Leaf's own sorry or Undetermined should read 'SORRY Demo.Leaf (an import of Demo.Down)', exit 1.
- After a replay over Leaf's source written again, the readers should read Leaf ok.

Add a timed-out build, and a failed one, of a module whose unlisted import's source was written with new bytes since its build. After the run, both readers should still read that import STALE.

While there, close the minor ones too: two listed modules sharing an unlisted import should give one line counted once; an info-level '✅ Expected Undetermined' should read ok; a `#print axioms` naming only sorryAx should read SORRY.

Then rerun the mutant set with these five mutants added, as the commit did for its 22.

findings.title: tally.py's new advice for a stale trace, 'run ./check.sh on it', fails for every module of tally.py's documented `Slice/Slice` use: `./check.sh Slice.X` reads FAILED
findings.scenario: A checkout or stash rewrites Slice/'s sources with the same bytes. `python3 -I tally.py Slice/Slice`, which README.md:182 documents, then prints 'NOT OK Slice.Rule: a trace older than its source (run ./check.sh on it)' for each of Slice's 10 modules. Following the advice, `./check.sh Slice.Rule` runs `lake build Slice.Rule` in the main package, where no library holds Slice.*. Lake answers 'unknown target', check.sh reads 'FAILED Slice.Rule (exit 1 …)', and the module stays NOT OK. The step that works is `./check.sh seedelf-slice Slice.Rule`, or `./check.sh seedelf-slice`. The README's '`./check.sh` on it settles the last' and tally.py's docstring ('`./check.sh <module>` rebuilds it or reads it again') say the same wrong step. No build is lost: forget() finds no Slice/Rule.lean at the root and removes nothing.
findings.evidence:
tally.py:129 `("a trace older than its source (run ./check.sh on it)", …)`. The same advice is at :122 (a trace that doesn't read), in the docstring at :13-15, and at README.md:182.

check.sh:44 `cd "$(dirname "$0")"` builds from the main package. Only `seedelf-slice` changes into Slice/ (check.sh:210-212).

Lake 4.24's `resolveTargetInWorkspace` (toolchain src/lean/lake/Lake/CLI/Build.lean:166-176) tries a target declaration, then a package, then `ws.findTargetModule?`, and otherwise throws `CliError.unknownTarget`. The main workspace's libraries are Seedelf, Lovejoin, Upstream and Audit (lakefile.lean) plus the three dependencies'. Slice is its own package (Slice/lakefile.lean), not a dependency of the main one.

Harness /tmp/claude-1000/-home-logic-Documents-LogicalMechanism-Seedelf-Wallet/0e0d3674-7c6c-46fb-8cae-a49695fa3bfe/scratchpad/r51/work/L4tools/h-slice.sh. Its stand-in lake resolves a module only when the package it runs in holds the source, as that function does.
1. tally.py Slice/Slice: 'NOT OK Slice.Rule: a trace older than its source (run ./check.sh on it)'.
2. './check.sh Slice.Rule: exit 1 :: FAILED Slice.Rule … :: unknown target `Slice.Rule`', and tally.py still reads NOT OK.
3. './check.sh seedelf-slice Slice.Rule: exit 0 :: ok', then '0 not ok'.

Real Lake wasn't run; its answer is traced from its source.
findings.fix: Have tally.py name the step for the package it reads: `./check.sh seedelf-slice <module>` when the lib argument is under Slice/, and `./check.sh <module>` otherwise. Say the same in its docstring and in README.md:182. count.py reads only the main package's audit families, so its advice holds.
findings.known_check: Searched the drafted record archive/plans/review-51.md (its 'Not run in the final checks: seedelf-slice'), docs/backlog.md, INDEX.md, FINDINGS.md, owner-calls.md and lanes/L3tests.md for seedelf-slice, 'Slice/Slice', 'run ./check.sh on it' and 'rebuild it'. Not recorded.

checked_ok: Lake 4.24 never reads a trace file's mtime. A replay needs depHash equal to the trace's and the artifacts to exist (Build/Common.lean, checkHashUpToDate and SavedTrace.replayIfUpToDate). `GetMTime Module` mixes the .olean, .ilean and .c (Config/Module.lean:210-212), and that is what old mode compares. So dating traces changes no Lake decision, even with --old.

A module's source hash comes fresh from its text on every build (Module.recFetchInput: `hash := .ofText contents`), never from a cached .hash. So 'Lake replays a log only for the source it was built from' holds, and the dating's premise is sound.

A moved pin can't replay under dating: whenever a dependency's HEAD differs from the manifest, Lake checks out the manifest's revision (Load/Materialize.lean:208-214), so the dependency's modules and every importer rebuild. What a moved pin leaves unbuilt outside any run stays as the README documents.

Dating happens only after rc=0 (check.sh:345), and a passed `lake build M` built or replayed every transitive import of M. So no trace judge() dates is one Lake didn't check in that build. A source written during the build reads STALE afterwards, because the stamp comes before the write (test-tools.sh's TT_EDIT case shows it).

The extract scripts write only .hex and .flat files, never .lean (extract.sh:40-41, extract-lovejoin.sh:62-63, extract-lovejoin-v2.sh:99-103). So dating hides no re-extraction the readers would otherwise have flagged. script-hex-not-lake-inputs stays as recorded.

judge()'s static import parse equals the imports Lake recorded in each trace (`X transitive imports (legacy)` and `X:importAllArts`) for all 676 root traces in FIXTREE: 0 mismatches. All 2,512 import lines are plain `import X`; there's no `import all`, `public import` or two modules on one line.

judge()'s counting rule flags none of FIXTREE's 679 root traces, and in dependencies only PlutusCore.UPLC.CekMachine, which is never judged. No trace has an 'Undetermined', a sorryAx axiom list or a synthetic (cache-fetch) entry. No LAKE_ variable or artifact cache is set.

Emulating judge() read-only for all 23 runs (the default, every named family, the 8 audit families) over FIXTREE finds 0 unlisted imports not ok, and no false NO TRACE. The import counts match the record: lovejoin 5, lovejoin-v2 12, lovejoin-any-tx 48, default 3 (Seedelf.Policy, Seedelf.Wallet, Seedelf.Signers.Keys); seedelf-every, lovejoin-every, upstream, upstream-main and seedelf-slice 0.

The bash side holds:
- judge()'s '- -', an empty output and a judge that stops all give NO TRACE and exit 1.
- An import that isn't ok gets its own line and fails the run, without changing its importer's line.
- A listed import is read only at its own turn.
- A dependency's module is never judged.
- The summary's count line is right.

count.py's default families are exactly run-all.sh's eight, so a full audit run now dates every module count.py reads: l3tests#2 is fixed. On FIXTREE after the final runs, tally.py Seedelf reads 2 not ok (PolicyBurn and PolicyMint, down from 158 before this commit) and Lovejoin 2 (the backlog's two modules no family builds). count.py reads 22 ok and 178 STALE, because the audit families weren't run, as the record says.

test-tools.sh passes on an unmodified copy: 41 ok in 4.6 s. Each check's assertions match its name; one is loose, 'tally.py: everything over Dep.Base rests on it', which asserts Side and Down but not Top. The new dating checks catch dating to judge()'s own clock and dating only the listed module.
The cost: judge()'s re-walk per module takes about 2 s over lovejoin-any-tx's 143 modules, and under 1 s for every other run.

The README's example import line has check.sh's format. The new STALE wording in Audit/README.md and count.py matches count.py's output. run-all.sh's five new checks each test the status rule they name.
notes: The once-a-run rule (check.sh:351) has one gap: an import judged during an earlier module's build isn't read again. If its source is edited mid-run and a later build rebuilds it with a sorry, the run exits 0, though Lake's fresh trace still shows the sorry to tally.py. check.sh's header says 'once a run', so this is by design. It's an edge only an edit during a run reaches.

Pre-existing, not from this commit: check.sh's usage line 40, './check.sh audit-quick  an audit family (Audit/audit-*.txt), then Audit/count.py', reads as if check.sh runs count.py. It doesn't; only run-all.sh does. The line has been there since a04ca256.

The Slice path of judge() and the dating has no real data here: FIXTREE's Slice/ has no .lake, and the final checks skipped seedelf-slice, as the record says. In fixtures it behaves like the main package.
The two Lovejoin AnyTx modules tally.py reads not ok are the backlog's ⬜ 'Two Lovejoin AnyTx modules no family builds'. Not re-reported, and nothing was done to them.

No money guards in this lens. The tool guards I met: check.sh:345 (only a passed build dates traces), pinned by no test (l4tools#1); check.sh:321 (the transitive walk), pinned by no test (l4tools#1); check.sh:347 (`|| judged=`), pinned by 'a judge that stops halfway'; check.sh:330 (the per-build stamp), pinned by 'a source written during its build reads stale after it'.
